question: There are two identical spherical solid balls of iron alloy touching each other. What would be the gravitational force of attraction between them if the density of the materials of the ball is (3 /2π) × 105 (kg/m3) and radius 1 m. G = 6.67 × 10-11Nm2/kg2.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**0.667 N**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The gravitational force of attraction between two spherical solid balls can be calculated using **Newton's law of gravitation**, which is given by the formula: **F = G * (m₁ * m₂) / d²**, where:

 
 
• **G** = Universal Gravitational Constant (6.67 × 10⁻¹¹ Nm²/kg²).
 
• **m₁** and **m₂** are the masses of the two spheres.
 
• **d** is the distance between the centers of the spheres.
